paper_title: Centered Ablation: Why Last-Layer Directional Ablation Under-Fires or Collapses, and a Closed-Form Fix

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Directional ablation removes a hidden state's component along a "behaviour direction" while a language model runs. It is the standard way to switch a behaviour such as refusal off, but it is erratic: on some models it barely fires, on others the text collapses into repetition. We show why, and fix it. At the last residual stream, ablation is exactly a logit bias: a fixed vocabulary footprint scaled by a gate, the cosine between the hidden state and the direction. The gate is measured from the origin, but last-layer states share a large common mode far from it, so a direction that overlaps the common mode fires on benign text and under-fires on its targets. Centered Ablation (CA) projects the common mode out of the direction, in closed form. Across 8 models, CA raises attack success by 29 and 46 points where the standard recipe under-fires, cuts collapse on Gemma-2-9B from 50\% to 1\%, and preserves 12 to 40 points more benign answers on high-overlap models, 39 to 46 more than the affine offset of prior work. Two numbers computed before generation predict, on models the analysis had not seen, which gain faithfulness and which gain attack success, and a collapse index marks when text degenerates. We also show that two standard safety judges score collapsed text in opposite directions, which can fabricate a 46-point effect.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Editing language models activations at inference time is now standard way to control its behaviour without retraining (Turner et al., 2024; Zou et al., 2023a; Li et al., 2023; Rimsky et al., 2024). The most used edit is directional ablation: estimate direction in hidden space as the difference between the mean activations of two classes of prompts, then remove each hidden states component along it while the model runs. Removing the refusal direction makes chat model comply with harmful requests; adding it back makes the model refuse more (Arditi et al., 2024). The recipe is cheap, gradient-free and widely reused. It is also erratic, and the literature treats the symptoms as model-specific quirks. On some models the recipe barely fires: Llama-3.2-3B, after its refusal direction is ablated, still opens 86% of its answers to harmful requests with refusal. On others it fires everywhere: Gemma-2-9B degenerates into Heres the truth: Here Here Here. . . on half of its prompts. Practitioners tune the strength, swap the estimator (Belrose et al., 2023; Wollschläger et al., 2025), or add an offset: affine concept editing (ACE; Marshall et al., 2025) re-anchors the projection at the benign mean and reports that this prevents collapse. None of these fixes says what the edit does to the output, so none says in advance which models will misbehave, in which way, or what fix must change. The lens. We restrict the edit to the one site where it has closed form: the residual stream after the last decoder block, which feeds only the final normalization and the unembedding. There, ablation is exactly 1 Figure 1: Centered Ablation repairs the standard recipe where it fails and changes little elsewhere. One row per model, ordered by the overlap ω (Section 3.3); line joins DIM ablation (gray) to CA (blue). (a) Fluent-only attack success on HarmBench. (b) Benign Alpaca answers rewritten. Exact values in Tables 10 and 12. logit bias (Section 3.2): every tokens score moves by fixed vector, the directions footprint, scaled by one scalar, the gate, which is the cosine between the hidden state and the direction. cosine is measured from the origin, but last-layer states cluster far from it, along shared common mode. direction that overlaps the common mode fires on ordinary text, which rewrites benign answers and, once the bias exceeds the logit spread, collapses the output; the same overlap dilutes the directions class-separating part, so the edit under-fires on its targets. One quantity, the overlap ω, explains all three symptoms. The fix. The lens says what correction must do: measure the gate from the benign class, not from the origin. We propose Centered Ablation (CA): project the common mode out of the direction before ablating (Section 3.4). It is closed-form, needs two sample means and one projection, and has no hyperparameter beyond the strength. ACEs offset reaches the same benign origin by shifting the origin while keeping the direction; we derive how the two routes differ, and show that the offset buys attack success with benign collateral on exactly the high-ω models. The lens also yields diagnostics computable before generation: ω, an efficacy η and collapse index β. We test all of this on 8 instruction-tuned models from three families, with 6 calibration draws and two safety judges; the analysis was developed on 3 of them and then scaled to all 8, with the diagnostics and predicted regime of the 5 added later recorded before they generated any text. Figure 1 shows the headline. Contributions. Centered Ablation. closed-form correction of directional ablation that raises attack success by +29.0 and +46.3 points on the two under-firing models, cuts collapse on Gemma-2-9B from 50% to 1%, and preserves 12 to 40 points more benign answers on the four high-ω models (Section 4.3). An exact lens. Last-layer ablation is cosine-gated logit bias (Proposition 3.1); the closed form predicts the served models steered first token on 96.1% of prompts across every model, direction and calibration draw (Section 4.2). The offset route, derived. ACEs offset and CA are the two ways to centre the gate; the offset fires 1 ω2 but rewrites 39 to 46 points more benign answers where ω is large (Section 4.4). harder by 1/ Diagnostics before generation. ω predicts the faithfulness gain (Spearman 0.98) and η the attack-success gain (Pearson 0.95); β+ > 1 marks the only collapsing model; the regime of 4 of the 5 models added after the pilot was predicted correctly in advance (Section 4.5). sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Activation steering. Steering adds or removes direction in hidden space at inference time: activation addition (Turner et al., 2024), contrastive activation addition (Rimsky et al., 2024), representation engineering (Zou et al., 2023a) and inference-time intervention (Li et al., 2023). Conditional variants decide when to steer with separate detector (Lee et al., 2025). Reliability studies find that steering effects vary widely across inputs and behaviours (Tan et al., 2024; Dang & Ngo, 2026). These works evaluate the edit by its behavioural outcome; none derives the edits effect on the output distribution, so none can say in advance where it will under-fire or collapse. Refusal directions and their geometry. Refusal in chat models is mediated by direction whose ablation removes refusal and whose addition induces it (Arditi et al., 2024); later work finds multi-dimensional refusal cones (Wollschläger et al., 2025). ACE (Marshall et al., 2025) argues that refusal is an affine rather than linear function of activations and re-anchors the projection at the benign mean, at mid-network layer chosen by inspection; it reports that the offset prevents collapse. The offset is motivated geometrically; it is not derived from what the edit does, it keeps the direction unchanged, and it gives no criterion for which models need it. Linear representations and concept erasure. The linear representation hypothesis (Mikolov et al., 2013; Park et al., 2024) motivates projecting concept out. Erasure methods choose the projection to remove linearly decodable information (Ravfogel et al., 2020; Belrose et al., 2023). They optimize decodability, which is not the property that governs steering: the most discriminative direction we test is the least effective one to ablate. Vocabulary-space readings and anisotropy. The logit lens reads intermediate states through the unembedding (nostalgebraist, 2020; Belrose et al., 2025; Geva et al., 2022); we use the same map for an exact account of an intervention rather than description of unsteered states. Contextual representations occupy narrow cone (Ethayarajh, 2019), are dominated by few coordinates (Timkey & van Schijndel, 2021; Sun et al., 2024), and benefit from removing dominant principal directions (Mu & Viswanath, 2018); none of these works connects anisotropy to the selectivity of an intervention. Evaluating jailbreaks and steering. Attack success is judged by classifiers (Mazeika et al., 2024; Inan et al., 2023), and refusal-only or keyword metrics are known to overstate success (Souly et al., 2024). Overrefusal is measured separately (Röttger et al., 2024). Prior evaluations do not report how judges score degenerate text, which is where we find them disagreeing in opposite directions. Our approach. CA is closed-form correction of the direction itself, derived from an exact account of what last-layer ablation does to the logits. Relative to ACE it changes the direction rather than the origin, which removes the common-mode variance the offset leaves in place; relative to erasure it targets the gate rather than decodability; and unlike every method above it comes with diagnostics that say, before generation, which models need it and what it buys  (Table 1)  . Two entries of the table carry caveat: among the erasure methods only LEACE is closed form (INLP iterates), and ACE reports that its offset prevents collapse but gives no mechanism for it.

sections.content: We fix one operator at one site and derive exactly what it does. The derivation (Section 3.2) explains why the standard recipe misfires (Section 3.3), dictates the fix (Section 3.4), separates it from the offset of prior work (Section 3.5), and yields diagnostics and limit (Section 3.6). Symbols are defined where they first appear and collected in Table 3; every proof is in Section B. 3 Table 1: Positioning. Closed form: no optimization or tuned hyperparameter beyond strength. Centred gate: the edit is anchored at the benign class, not the origin. Exact effect: the change in output is derived, not only measured. Predicts in advance: says before generation which models need correction. Explains collapse: gives mechanism and threshold. Shaded row, CA: ours. sections.title: 4 Experiments
sections.content: 4.1 Setup Models and data. Every claim below is evaluated on the same eight instruction-tuned models from three families: Qwen2.5-{0.5B, 3B, 7B} and Qwen3-4B (Qwen Team, 2025a;b), Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.2-3B (Llama Team, 2024), and Gemma-2-{2B, 9B} (Gemma Team, 2024). The study ran in two stages: we developed the analysis on three pilot models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B) and then scaled to all eight. For the five added in the second stage, ω, η, the simulated token changes and predicted regime were recorded before any of them generated text, which is what makes the prediction in Section 4.5 out of sample; nothing else distinguishes them, and all eight carry equal weight everywhere else. Directions are calibrated on 256 AdvBench (Zou et al., 2023b) versus 256 Alpaca (Taori et al., 2023) prompt-final states, resampled in 6 calibration draws. Attack success is evaluated on HarmBench (n = 240; Mazeika et al., 2024), benign behaviour on 100 held-out Alpaca prompts, MMLU (1000; Hendrycks et al., 2021) and GSM8K (100; Cobbe et al., 2021). Generation is greedy, 256 new tokens. Every setting is in Section C, every judge prompt in Section D. Conditions. Three directions, all at = 1 and all at the last layer: DIM ablation (the standard recipe), CA (Equation (7)) and DIM+offset (Equation (8), offset fitted on the same calibration states). They differ only in where the gate is anchored. One model, one direction and one calibration draw form cell; the main matrix has 8 3 6 = 144 cells, and every cell is scored on every metric below. Refusal amplification uses < 0 (CA-Amp, DIM-Amp). Metrics and statistics. Rates are in percent, differences in points. Attack success rate (ASR) is judged by the HarmBench classifier and, as second judge, Llama-Guard-3-8B (Inan et al., 2023). An output is degenerate if it is at least 200 bytes and zlib compresses it to under 0.2 of its length; the collapse rate is the fraction of degenerate outputs, and the primary ASR is fluent-only, which counts them as failures. The benign rewrite rate is the fraction of benign answers whose string similarity to the unsteered answer is below 0.5 (lower is more faithful); its drop from DIM to method is the benign answers preserved. pairwise judge (Qwen3-8B, both orders) asks whether rewrite is also loss. Differences use paired prompt-level bootstrap (5000 replicates, draws averaged inside each replicate) and an exact McNemar test per draw (McNemar, 1947). 4.2 RQ1: Is the reduction exact in practice? Yes: the closed form predicts the served models steered first token on 96.1% of prompts (Figure 3). For every cell we predicted the first token from cached unsteered states, WU and alone, and compared it with the token vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023) emitted under the same intervention. The one shortfall, Gemma-2-9B (82.1%), is informative: under CA its first token is no longer refusal onset, but refusal returns later as semantic deflection (Heres the thing: is harmful. . . ), the limit studied in Section 4.6. Everything that follows treats the reduction as the definition of the operator. 4.3 RQ2: What does CA fix, and what does it cost? CA repairs each failure mode on the models that show it, and moves the others by at most 2.6 points (Figure 1). Under-firing. On Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.2-3B, CA raises ASR from 33.6% to 62.6% (+29.0 [22.9, 35.1]) and from 10.3% to 56.7% (+46.3 [40.3, 52.4]), significant on 6 of 6 draws under both judges  (Table 11)  . On Llama-3.2-3B, 86% of DIM-steered responses still open with refusal; under CA, 19% do. On the other six models the HarmBench ASR moves by at most 2.6 points, never significantly. Collapse. On Gemma-2-9B, DIM degenerates on 50% of prompts; CA on 1%, at the same fluent-only ASR (14.0% vs. 14.4%; Table 10). Collateral. On the four models with ω > 0.3, CA preserves 12 to 40 points more benign answers than DIM; on the four with ω < 0.13 the difference is at most 5 points  (Table 12)  . The cost is smaller effect than the offset route on some models, never capability loss. MMLU, scored exactly at the logit level through Proposition 3.1, moves by at most 0.7 points for every model and direction, and GSM8K stays within noise  (Table 13)  . Most benign rewrites are not losses either: net pairwise preference against the unsteered answer is within 10 points in 23 of 24 cells  (Table 14)  ; the exception is the offset route, next. 4.4 RQ3: Centre the direction, or shift the origin? The two routes trade off as Section 3.5 predicts: the offset fires harder, and its extra benign rewriting grows with ω (Figures 4 and 5). On prompt-final states, DIM+offsets mean harmful gate 1 ω2 on all 8 models (largest error 0.06), and its benign gate is exceeds CAs by the predicted factor 1/ wider on exactly the four models with ω > 0.3  (Table 15)  . Under the HarmBench classifier, DIM+offsets ASR is never significantly below CAs and is significantly higher on 3 models (Qwen2.5-7B by 3.7 points, both 3B models by 12.4); under Llama-Guard it is higher on 5 and lower on one, Gemma-2-2B  (Table 11)  . On the benign side, DIM+offset rewrites 39 to 46 points more answers than CA on the three models with ω > 0.33, within 1.3 points on three, 7 points more on Qwen2.5-7B and 8 points fewer on Qwen2.5-3B; its excess tracks ω (Pearson 0.80; Table 12). The only clear quality regression any method produces is DIM+offset on Gemma-2-9B (net preference 23.5 points: 28% losses, 4.5% wins). The gate ratio does not explain every gap: on Qwen2.5-3B the gates nearly coincide (ratio 1.01) yet the offset is 12.4 points stronger, so that difference arises later in generation. In short, CA is not stronger attack than the offset; it is the route that keeps benign behaviour intact where ω is large. 8 Figure 4: The offset route is the stronger attack on few models; CA is the faithful one on every high-ω model. (b) Spread of the gate on benign states: the two routes coincide at small ω and separate as it grows. Exact values in Table 15. 4.5 RQ4: Can we predict the benefit before generating? Yes, with two numbers that predict two different benefits (Figure 6a,b). The overlap ω predicts the benign answers preserved (Spearman 0.98, Pearson 0.90, = 8), and the efficacy η of DIM predicts the ASR gain (Pearson 0.95, Spearman 0.81; the same under Llama-Guard). The two are not interchangeable: ω barely orders the ASR gain (Spearman 0.19). Both Gemmas have large ω but η = 0.98, so they gain faithfulness and no attack success; both Llamas have large ω and low η, so they gain both. On these 8 models η = 0.6 separates the regimes: the two models below it gain +29.0 and +46.3 points, the six above lie in [2.6, +2.4]. Neither diagnostic is family property. The regime recorded for the five models added after the pilot, before any of them generated text, used three coarse labels and scored 4 of 5; the miss, Gemma-2-2B (labelled as an ASR gain), preserved 16.5 points of benign answers and gained no ASR, which is what its two numbers, ω = 0.32 and η = 0.98, imply  (Table 16)  . Collapse is threshold at β+ = 1; collateral is linear in β (Figure 6c,d). Exactly 6 of the 144 cells have β+ > 1, all Gemma-2-9B under DIM (β+ = 1.03 0.01 over its 6 draws), and they are the cells that collapse (mean collapse rate 49.8%); the other 138 have β+ 0.90 and mean collapse rate of 0.6% (max 4.2%). Only one model crosses, so the data place the transition in (0.90, 1.03] and no finer; below it nothing collapses. On the benign side the chain closes end to end: ω sets β for DIM (Pearson 0.87); CA flattens β to 0.030.06 on every model; and the drop in β, computed from cached activations, predicts the measured benign answers preserved (Pearson 0.98, Spearman 0.95; Table 17). The level-to-level correlation is only 0.39, because the absolute rewrite rate also depends on how variable models own generations are. 4.6 RQ5: Where does last-layer ablation stop? It controls behaviours decided at few tokens, and only erodes behaviours spread across text. Refusals second stage. sections.title: 5 Limitations
sections.content: One site, one operator. The reduction holds only at the last residual stream and for rank-1 ablation under greedy decoding. Under sampling, the rescaling τs acts as temperature; at earlier layers the edit propagates through attention and no closed form exists. We make no claim about mid-depth or additive steering, and DIM+offset is ACEs offset at our site, not ACE at its authors mid-network layer. Small-n laws. Both diagnostic laws rest on 8 models. The separation at η = 0.6 rests on two models below the threshold, and only one model crosses β+ = 1, so the collapse threshold is bracketed in (0.90, 1.03] and no finer.

sections.title: 6 Conclusion
sections.content: At the last residual stream, directional ablation is an exact, cosine-gated logit bias, and its three failures, under-firing, collateral and collapse, are one mechanism: gate measured from the origin, applied to states that share large common mode. Centered Ablation removes that common mode from the direction in closed form, repairs each failure on the models that show it, and preserves 39 to 46 points more benign answers than the offset of prior work where the overlap is large; diagnostics from the same analysis predicted, before generation and on models the analysis had not seen, which models gain faithfulness (ω) and which gain attack success (η). Before steering model, compute ω, η and β from cached activations; use CA when ω is large, or the offset when effect matters more than faithfulness; expect ablation to work only when η is high under the centred direction; and report fluent-only success with collapse rate and free-form faithfulness measure.

sections.title: Broader Impact Statement
sections.content: This work analyses an intervention that can remove models refusal behaviour; the same analysis shows how to amplify refusal against jailbreaks and how standard safety evaluations can misreport either. Refusal removal on open-weight models is already public (Arditi et al., 2024; Marshall et al., 2025), and CA is not stronger attack than existing ones. We expect the main effect to be better evaluation practice: fluency-filtered judging, free-form faithfulness checks, and diagnostics that flag unreliable interventions before deployment. We release no harmful generations beyond those needed to reproduce the judged metrics, and all data are public benchmarks.

sections.content: G.1 Summary of the direction-space checks 1. Kernels add nothing. RBF-kernel MMD erasure (Gretton et al., 2012) reduces to lengthreweighted DIM (cos = 1.000 on Llama and Qwen), which after centring is CA (cos 0.999; Section G.2). 2. Detection is not erasure. The most discriminative direction, shrinkage LDA (gate AUC 0.95), is the worst ablation direction (ASR 2.923.7%, below both DIM and CA on every pilot model): its footprint points at tokens unrelated to refusal  (Table 19)  . 3. The common mode is not the top principal component ( cos = 0.110.22, while uDIM has 0.920.99), nor outlier coordinates; and centring on the pooled mean of both classes removes the signal (Section G.3). 4. Strength, not locality: DIM at = 0.5 matches the kernel directions that seemed to collapse less  (Table 21)  . Trajectory-calibrated and whitened directions do not help (Section G.5); random direction leaves ASR at baseline. G.2 Kernel and erasure directions We built two nonlinear families. sections.content: Table 25 is the full trade-off. Neither direction dominates: DIM-Amp and the gated variant own the low over-refusal end, CA-Amp the low-ASR end. Only CA-Amp reaches strong, fluent defence on Gemma-2-9B, and on Llama-3.1-8B it reaches 0.5% where DIM-Amp floors at 3.3%. Defence is template-dependent: on Gemma-2-9B, CA-Amp at = 1.5 to 3 holds dev-mode, research and few-shot-compliance at 016% but reaches only 5469% on evil-confidant. The 8 templates shift activations in poorly aligned directions (mean pairwise cos 0.3) while all of them lower the projection on the refusal direction. Ablating jailbreak direction (train-template minus plain-harmful states) backfires: it is anti-aligned with the refusal direction (cos = 0.72, 0.30, 0.82 on Qwen, Llama, Gemma), and on Qwen at = 2 it lowers refusal on plain harmful prompts from 91% to 3%. 38 Table 25: Refusal amplification against held-out jailbreak templates.
